title: [finding] The gantt link guard's `group` branch is unreachable: a `type:'group'` row renders no bar, so the drag can never target it
body:
Measured while implementing objectui#4158 (PR for the link-rejection feedback) — **not in that card's scope**, which is user feedback for the guard's verdicts, not an audit of the verdicts themselves. Observation-class: nothing a user hits today, and the guard is not wrong — the branch simply cannot fire. ## The branch `packages/plugin-gantt/src/GanttView.tsx`, the built-in drop-target policy, refuses four kinds of dependency link. One of them: ```js if (target.type === 'group') return 'group'; ``` ## Why it cannot fire The policy is consulted from exactly two places, both on the drag-to-link path: `captureLinkTarget` (a bar registering itself as the hover target) and the release handler. Both require a **bar** to exist for the target row. A `type: 'group'` row renders none. From the row renderer: ```js if (task.type === 'group') { // 分组层级 (项目/产品): a pure tree header — the left list still // shows the caret + label, but the timeline row carries NO bar. return (
{tooltip}
); } ``` So for a group row there is no bar to hover, nothing that can call `captureLinkTarget`, and the row's own `onPointerMove` is `clearLinkTarget` — which actively *clears* any target. The branch is dead on this path. Note the neighbouring case does **not** cover it: `row.isSummary` (a task with children, or `type: 'summary'`) does render a bar and does register as a drop target — and the policy accepts it, because `isSummary` is not `type === 'group'`. So "you cannot link to a summary row" is not what the code does; only the explicit `group` type is refused, and only that type renders no bar. The `type: 'group'` check sits *before* the `isSummary` branch in the renderer, so a group row can never take the bar path either. ## Why it is not simply dead code to delete Two directions, and the choice is a product question rather than a cleanup: - **The branch is cheap insurance.** If a group row ever gains a bar — or a second link-creation path appears that does not go through bar hover — the branch starts firing and is correct. - **But an unreachable branch cannot be tested end-to-end**, and #4158 now attaches a user-visible message to it (`gantt.link.rejected.group`, ten packs). That message is deliberately kept: without it the branch would render the raw key `gantt.link.rejected.group` on screen if it ever did fire, which is strictly worse than an unused string. The #4158 PR pins the reachability fact instead, so the test goes red the day group rows gain a bar. ## The adjacent question worth asking The context-menu path (`Add predecessor…` / `Add successor…` → dependency picker) creates links **without** consulting this policy at all — it is a separate call site that does not call `canReceiveLink`. Whether the picker should offer group rows as candidates, and whether it should be subject to the same four-branch policy as the drag path, is a real question this finding does not answer. That is the direction in which the `group` branch might actually acquire a reachable meaning. ## Options - **A. Leave it.** The branch is correct-but-dormant, and #4158's test now pins the reason. Zero cost, keeps the insurance. - **B. Route the context-menu picker through the same policy.** Gives the branch a live meaning and closes the inconsistency between the two link-creation paths. Needs a product call on whether the picker should *filter* illegal candidates or *reject* them with the same toast. - **C. Remove the branch and its message.** Cleanest by enforce-or-remove, but it deletes the insurance and would have to be re-added the moment either of the above changes. Recommendation: **A for now, B as its own card if the picker/drag inconsistency is judged worth closing** — B is the only one that turns the branch from dormant into meaningful, but it is a behaviour change to a second interaction and deserves its own scope rather than riding a feedback card. Related: objectui#4158 (the feedback card that measured this). --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_017Qqyix2QcnpUC9XeYVDzx3)_
